title: Works in Public 2026 Unveiling
description: The Art Students League of New York and the New York City Department of Parks & Recreation are proud to present Works in Public 2026 , a year-long outdoor public art exhibition in Riverside Park. The exhibition features four new site-specific sculptures by League artists: Alicia Ehni and Robert Franca in Riverside Park South at 61st Street, and Lindsey Francis Jones and Clare Burson in Riverside Park North at 145th Street. Schedule: 1:45pm – Meet in Riverside Park North, 145th St. to unveil the new rosk by Lindsey Francis Jones and Clare Burson. 3:00pm – Board our free shuttle to Riverside Park South 3:45pm – Arrive at Riverside Park South, 61st St to unveil the new works by Alicia Ehni and Robert Franca. About the Art and Artists: Lindsey Francis Jones, City in Shapes, City in Fish City in Shapes, City in Fish invites viewers into the artist’s visual language through a cityscape of abstract shapes and color. Inspired by the craft and community of printmaking, the work incorporates images of six fish etched onto selected plexiglass, contributed by fellow printmakers and artists: Laurissa Widrick, Felix Bladbjerg, Kait Waldman, Stan Overstreet, Barbara Ganmen, and Scarlett Patino. Clare Burson, Unearthed . UNEARTHED is an installation of three steel forms inspired by the ancient Plain of Jars in Laos. It asks us to consider the inevitable and unexpected ways that history imposes itself on the present. When experienced with its accompanying soundscape, UNEARTHED also reminds us that our shared public spaces are nexus points for an infinite number of narratives that connect individuals and communities across time, those who lived here before us and those who will come after us. Alicia Ehni, Balancing A Peruvian shaman once told Ehni to carry a lemon in her purse, that it brings great harmony in life and in interactions with others. Two fractured pre-Columbian ceramics carry ancient coastal knowledge, opening possibilities to imagine a different future. Balancing reflects on the fragile relationships between people, nature, and the built environment. Robert Franca, The Chairs The Chairs explores family as the foundation through which we understand ourselves and the world. Seen through a child’s perspective, the chairs embody imagination, openness, and freedom from conventional rules. Their human-like forms suggest movement and the ability to change. Ultimately, the chairs speak to the importance of finding balance — within ourselves, within families, and in navigating the challenges and uncertainties of an ever-changing world.

title: Riverfront Ramble
description: Put down your phone and get outside for the inaugural Riverfront Ramble , presented by Riverside Park Conservancy , Palisades Parks Conservancy , and Fort Tryon Park Conservancy . This free cross-river walking adventure and scavenger hunt invites people of all ages to explore Fort Washington Park, Palisades Interstate Park, and Fort Tryon Park . Become a “Riverfront Rambler” and cross the George Washington Bridge on foot in search of landmarks, scenic overlooks, and other points of interest. Leave your screen behind, follow a paper map, and discover the parks at your own pace. Ramblers can pick up a free map at any of three staffed hubs: The Little Red Lighthouse in Fort Washington Park The N.J. entrance to the G.W.B. North Walk and the Palisades Interstate Park Long Path The Cottage at Fort Tryon Park Maps and information will also be available at Break Away Cafe, 71 Cabrini Boulevard . Start in any park and choose to explore one, two, or all three. Along the way, check off what you discover and collect a unique rubber stamp and small keepsake at each park hub to mark your journey. We hope you’ll join us for this free, all ages event and opportunity to step away from the screen, get moving, and see the riverfront in a whole new way! Please RSVP here .

title: PlacePartner Opportunity: Compost Compound at W 95th St
description: The Conservancy’s Sustainability team invites you to support us with compost processing and gardening work and at the 95th Street Compost Compound. The compost that is currently in progress at our site is created right here in Riverside Park! We utilize machinery for the composting work, and when the compost is ready it will be applied to soil in the Park, thus retaining nutrients from the debris that enters the site and ‘closing the loop’. PlacePartner Opportunities are weekly/monthly occasions for volunteers to work alongside our field staff and ParkTenders . We will provide all the tools you need! Please bring water to stay hydrated. Please wear weather-appropriate clothing and closed-toed shoes. Please note that volunteers under 15 must be accompanied by an adult. For existing volunteers: Please sign up through the Grassroots Volunteer Portal . For new volunteers: Please email grassroots@riversideparknyc.org for information about how to get involved. This event is not suitable for corporate groups! If you are a corporate group, please email danny@riversideparknyc.org to set up a project.

title: ¡EN ESPAÑOL! Tree Club del Bosque de West Harlem
description: ¡Sea parte de Tree Club del Bosque de West Harlem! Fecha: Cuarto sábado Hora: 1:30 pm a 3:00 pm Lugar de reunión: W 143rd St y Riverside Drive Detalles del proyecto: Durante este evento, trabajaremos juntos para limpiar el parque, desmalezar y eliminar especies introducidas y cuidar nuestros árboles. Esto es parte de un nuevo proyecto de restauración llamado Bosque de West Harlem. ¡Ven a aprender y a restaurar 7.5 acres con nosotros! No se necesita experiencia, ¡solo trae tu energía y entusiasmo! Le proporcionaremos todas las herramientas y equipos necesarios. No olvides llevar ropa cómoda y zapatos cerrados(como botas o tenis), y llevar una botella de agua para mantenerte hidratado. ¡Este proyecto no es apto para grupos corporativos! Si es un grupo corporativo, envíe un correo electrónico a danny@riversideparknyc.org para configurar un proyecto.
